content: Fexofenadine is a medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis, commonly known as hay fever. These symptoms include a runny nose, sneezing, red or itchy eyes, watery eyes, and itching in areas such as the nose, throat, or roof of the mouth. It is also used to treat urticaria, which presents as hives or red, itchy, raised areas on the skin, along with associated itching and rashes. This medication is suitable for adults and children aged 2 years and older for allergic rhinitis, and for urticaria, it can be used in children as young as 6 months. Fexofenadine belongs to a class of drugs called antihistamines, which work by blocking the effects of histamine, a chemical in the body responsible for allergy symptoms. Fexofenadine is available in tablet form or as a liquid suspension, both of which are taken orally. It is typically taken once or twice daily with water. It is important to avoid consuming fruit juices such as orange, grapefruit, or apple juice when taking this medication, as they can reduce its effectiveness. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than directed. While fexofenadine helps control the symptoms of allergic rhinitis and urticaria, it does not cure these conditions. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well and are not experiencing symptoms, as skipping doses may worsen your condition. Fexofenadine may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about additional uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting fexofenadine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, any of its ingredients, or any other drugs. Your pharmacist can provide a list of the ingredients if needed. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. If you are using antacids containing aluminum or magnesium, take them a few hours before or after fexofenadine to avoid interactions. Inform your doctor if you have a history of kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, discuss this with your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking fexofenadine, notify your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you can continue your normal diet while taking fexofenadine. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Fexofenadine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include headache, dizziness, diarrhea, vomiting, pain in the arms, legs, or back, general pain, menstrual pain, and cough. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, hoarseness, and difficulty swallowing or breathing. If you experience any of these severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. If you notice any other unusual problems while taking this medication, inform your doctor. Store fexofenadine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include dizziness, drowsiness, and dry mouth. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Fexofenadine is sold under the brand name Allegra®.
